title: Collect employee names into an unmodifiable list, and build an id-to-name lookup as an unmodifiable map, using `Collectors.collectingAndThen` to apply a finishing step. Explain how `collectingAndThen` wraps a collector with a final transformation and why it is used for immutability.
shortTitle: Build an immutable lookup map and an unmodifiable list using Collectors.collectingAndThen

s1_definition.profdef: `Collectors.collectingAndThen(downstream, finisher)` runs a downstream collector and then applies a finishing function to its result. It is commonly used to make a mutable collection immutable, for example collecting into a list and then wrapping it with `Collections.unmodifiableList`, in a single collect call.
s1_definition.analogy: Priya gathers names into a notebook (the list), then as the last step she laminates the page so nobody can edit it (unmodifiable). collectingAndThen is "collect first, then do one final thing to the whole result".
s1_definition.oneliner: `collectingAndThen(collector, finisher)` collects, then transforms the finished result once — ideal for returning immutable collections.
s1_definition.raw:
**Professional definition:** `Collectors.collectingAndThen(downstream, finisher)` runs a downstream collector and then applies a finishing function to its result. It is commonly used to make a mutable collection immutable, for example collecting into a list and then wrapping it with `Collections.unmodifiableList`, in a single collect call.

**In simple words (banking analogy):** Priya gathers names into a notebook (the list), then as the last step she laminates the page so nobody can edit it (unmodifiable). collectingAndThen is "collect first, then do one final thing to the whole result".

**One line to remember:** `collectingAndThen(collector, finisher)` collects, then transforms the finished result once — ideal for returning immutable collections.

sections.s2_technical:
`collectingAndThen(downstream, finisher)` first performs the downstream collection, then passes the completed result through the finisher function exactly once. The classic use is immutability: `collect(collectingAndThen(toList(), Collections::unmodifiableList))` returns a list that throws `UnsupportedOperationException` on modification, which protects shared data from accidental mutation.

A worked finance example for a lookup: `collect(collectingAndThen(toMap(Employee::getId, Employee::getName), Collections::unmodifiableMap))` builds an id-to-name map and seals it. The finisher can also be any transformation, such as wrapping a result or extracting a single value from a collected structure.

The senior nuance is that in modern JDKs `Collectors.toUnmodifiableList`, `toUnmodifiableSet`, and `toUnmodifiableMap` exist and are the preferred shorthands for the immutability case, and they reject nulls. collectingAndThen remains valuable when the finisher is something other than simple wrapping — for instance collecting into a list and then returning its size, or collecting into a map and then adapting it. The finisher runs once on the whole result, not per element, so it is cheap.
sections.s3_banking:
Problem 1 — The National Bank of India loads a reference list of employee names once at startup and shares it across threads. If any part of the code accidentally added or removed a name, it would corrupt the shared reference, so the list must be immutable after it is built.

Problem 2 — The same startup builds an id-to-name lookup map that many services read. It too must be sealed so no reader can mutate it.

This is exactly what collectingAndThen does — it collects the names into a list and the entries into a map, then as a finishing step wraps each in an unmodifiable view, all in one collect call.

The code defines `Employee`, a `ReferenceDataService` with `immutableNames` and `immutableLookup`, and a demo.
sections.s4a_structure:
```
reference-data-service/
├── pom.xml
└── src/main/java/com/bank/refdata/
    ├── RefDataDemo.java
    ├── model/Employee.java
    └── service/ReferenceDataService.java
```
sections.s5_journey:
Input: three employees — Rajesh (1), Priya (2), Amit (3).

Step 1: For names, map extracts each name and toList gathers a mutable list of Rajesh, Priya, Amit.

Step 2: The finisher wraps that list with unmodifiableList, producing a sealed view.

Step 3: For the lookup, toMap builds a mutable map of id to name.

Step 4: The finisher wraps it with unmodifiableMap, sealing it too.

Step 5: Reading works — lookup of id 2 returns Priya — but any attempt to add to the names list throws UnsupportedOperationException, which the demo catches and logs.

```
INFO: Names: [Rajesh, Priya, Amit]
INFO: Lookup id=2: Priya
WARNING: Immutable list rejected modification as expected
```
sections.s5b_flow:
```
  employees
    │ map(name) → toList()  → [Rajesh, Priya, Amit]  (mutable)
    │ collectingAndThen finisher: Collections::unmodifiableList
    ▼
  [Rajesh, Priya, Amit]  (sealed — add() throws)

    │ toMap(id, name) → {1=Rajesh, 2=Priya, 3=Amit}  (mutable)
    │ finisher: Collections::unmodifiableMap
    ▼
  {1=Rajesh, 2=Priya, 3=Amit}  (sealed)
```
sections.s5c_hld:
```
  ═══ HLD — Immutable Reference Data at Startup ═══

  ┌──────────┐ startup ┌────────────────────┐ JDBC ┌────────────┐
  │ App Boot │────────→│ ReferenceDataService│───→│ PostgreSQL │
  └──────────┘         │ collect→seal        │    │ employees  │
                       └─────────┬──────────┘    └────────────┘
                                 ▼ shared across threads (read-only)
                          immutable names + id→name lookup
```
sections.s5d_lld:
```
  ═══ LLD — collectingAndThen ═══

  ┌─ collectingAndThen(downstream, finisher) ─────────────────┐
  │ 1. run downstream collector (toList / toMap)              │
  │ 2. apply finisher ONCE to the whole result                │
  │ immutability: finisher = Collections::unmodifiableList/Map │
  │ modern shorthand: toUnmodifiableList/Set/Map (reject null) │
  │ finisher can also transform / extract (e.g. return size)   │
  └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

  ┌───────────────────────────────┐
  │      ReferenceDataService     │
  │  + immutableNames(List):List  │ collectingAndThen(toList, unmod)
  │  + immutableLookup(List):Map  │ collectingAndThen(toMap, unmod)
  └───────────────────────────────┘

  Call chain:
  1. map/toMap collect (mutable)
  2. finisher seals result
  3. return read-only view
```
sections.s6_takeaway:
collectingAndThen wraps a collector with a finishing step: it runs the downstream collector first and then applies a function to the completed result exactly once. The most common use is immutability — I collect into a list or a map and then, as the finishing step, wrap it with Collections unmodifiableList or unmodifiableMap, so the returned collection rejects any modification. All of that happens in a single collect call.

In my banking project at the National Bank of India we loaded reference data once at startup — a list of employee names and an id-to-name lookup map — and shared it across threads. Because shared data must not be mutated accidentally, I sealed both with collectingAndThen, so any stray add or remove throws UnsupportedOperationException instead of silently corrupting the reference data.

The senior point I always mention is that modern JDKs offer toUnmodifiableList, toUnmodifiableSet, and toUnmodifiableMap as direct shorthands for the immutability case, and they also reject nulls, so I prefer them when I just need an immutable collection. I keep collectingAndThen for when the finisher is something richer than simple wrapping — for example collecting into a structure and then extracting a single derived value — since the finisher runs once on the whole result and is cheap.
